deliverables: Ongoing maintenance including bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, and releases
Initial Plutus V4 support in the compiler and standard library for a Dijkstra developer preview
Improved interfaces and documentation for JS/TS components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution
Runtime foundational components and reactive workers
Dijkstra ledger rules and transaction-builder updates including new builtins, cost models, nested transactions, accounts, and guard scripts
Java/Kotlin integration with Spring Boot and Ktor examples
Cleaner integration paths with Cardano Client Lib and Yaci
Runtime chain follower and task scheduler
request.what: Funding for a 9-month continuation of Scalus covering maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, JVM and JS/TS interoperability, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
Scalus is used directly by Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm systems.
Scalus components are embedded in Cardano Client Lib, YaciDevKit, MeshJS SDK, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution.
The proposal states Scalus has 4,642 commits across 32 releases, 12 contributors, and Scalus.js receives more than 20,000 downloads per month.
The requested budget is ₳2,464,844 for 9 months, based on a $0.16/ADA reference rate and no contingency.

This resubmission reduces the prior proposal from ₳8.5M over 12 months to about ₳2.464M over 9 months and removes the standalone L1 node, full L2 integration, and broad formal verification from scope.
The proposal says delivery will be milestone-based and administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.

The funded scope includes maintenance, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a first scoped application runtime, while excluding a production-grade JVM L1 node, full Gummiworm L2 integration, broad formal verification, and advanced devnet expansion.
Lantr Engineering says it previously delivered every Scalus milestone on time and commits to public reporting, community sessions, and on-time milestone delivery for this treasury-funded work.
The proposal frames Scalus as shared Apache 2.0 open-source infrastructure intended to reduce repeated assembly work across Cardano teams and tools.

summary: The proposal requests ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus for 9 months, focused on maintenance, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a scoped runtime, with claims of existing ecosystem reuse, reduced scope from a prior larger ask, milestone-based delivery, and third-party oversight.
